sentences.text: The genus is known only from fragmentary coracoid bones, which are parts of the shoulder girdle.
One species, I. silvae, was estimated to be 135 mm long, while I. martini reached 220 mm.
Fossils of Incolornis were discovered in the Bissekty Formation in Uzbekistan.
Incolornis is classified within the parent group Alexornithidae.
It also belongs to the family Alexornithidae.
The systematic position of Incolornis is unclear, though it may belong to the Enantiornithes.
Incolornis lived during the Coniacian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 89 and 86 million years ago.
However, the time range for the genus is estimated from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
